title: The problem RAG solves: knowledge the model does not have

videos.script: Ask a model how many days you have to return a printed book to Marginalia. It answers about a library: one to three weeks, and fines if you are late. {{closed}} It sounds sure, and it is about a different business. Marginalia gives thirty days. {{stale}} The model was never shown the shop's policy. Nobody trained it on your company's documents. {{never}} So give it the document. Paste the policy into the prompt and ask again. Now it says thirty days. {{with}} Why not paste everything, then? Because everything does not fit, and every question would pay to read all of it. {{full}} The answer is to search first. Find the few passages that matter, and send only those. {{loop}} That is retrieval-augmented generation, and this lesson builds the smallest one that works, in twenty lines, on your own machine. {{tiny}} Then it breaks it. A search can find last year's policy, and the model will quote it. Given nothing that answers, the model can still invent a rule. {{fails}} Each of those failures has a lesson of its own later in the course. {{end}}
